Can your architecture defend against attacks that are autonomous,
adaptive, and faster than anything you've seen before?

Frontier AI models are compressing the attack lifecycle and enabling a
new generation of agentic threats. Security teams must prepare for
faster, automated, and adaptive attacks.

Join Cato's CEO Shlomo Kramer and VP of Threat Intelligence Etay Maor
on June 3 to:

articles.title: Cursor hits $3 billion annual sales rate ahead of spacex deal
articles.description:
Cursor's annualized revenue hit $3 billion in late April. The company
now has more than 3,000 customers paying at least $100,000 each for
its software on an annualized basis. The business has become one of
the fastest-growing startups of all time. SpaceX has the right to buy
Cursor for $60 billion during a 30-day window that starts soon after
it begins trading publicly. SpaceX is expected to list its shares on
June 12.

articles.title: Manus weighs raising $1 billion to unwind meta takeover
articles.description:
Manus has been told to unwind its acquisition by Meta by China's
regulators. Its founders now need to raise funds to buy back the
operation. They are now in discussions for funding and may chip in
with their own money to finance the transaction. A reversal of a deal
this large months after completion is virtually unheard of. 

 ANTHROPIC, MICROSOFT IN TALKS FOR AI CHIP DEAL AFTER $5 BILLION

articles.title: Investment
articles.description:
Microsoft plans to supply its Maia AI chips to Anthropic, which
currently faces compute challenges despite partnerships with Amazon
and Google. Anthropic's increasing AI-assisted programming needs could
benefit from Maia's 30% improved performance. A $5 billion investment
by Microsoft in November strengthens this potential collaboration.

articles.title: Lessons learned from building cloud agents
articles.description:
Cursor described lessons from building cloud agents, emphasizing
durable execution, isolated development environments, self-healing
infrastructure, and cleaner separation between agent state and
conversation state.

articles.title: Ai's plummeting prices are a software story, not a hardware one
articles.description:
Local, open-weight models running on older commodity hardware are
becoming more and more competitive with models on the frontier. This
has big implications for what frontier labs will be able to charge for
their biggest models. Many applications don't need the best models, so
it's not worth paying the premium.

articles.title: Frontier labs don't use most ai compute (yet)
articles.description:
The current rate of scaling compute isn't sustainable unless AI
starts to dramatically accelerate economic growth. There is no
guarantee that this rate of AI capex spending can continue after 2026.
However, flat compute capex is still growing the compute stock for
years. AI chips will still improve, and companies can research and
train models even with a fixed amount of compute. 

🧑‍💻

articles.title: Datadog's best practices for llm observability
articles.description:
It's 10 o'clock. Do you know where your LLMs are? In this Datadog
guide [13], you'll learn how to monitor LLM workflows end-to-end,
detect security risks, and deploy mitigation steps. You don't need to
be on high alert if your system is reliable. Read the guide to see how
to build out LLM observability [13]

articles.title: Qwen3.7: the agent frontier
articles.description:
Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3.7-Max as a proprietary
agent-foundation model that posts top scores on Terminal-Bench
2.0-Terminus, SWE-Pro, SciCode, MCP-Mark, GPQA Diamond, HMMT Feb 2026,
and IMOAnswerBench, with consistent performance across Claude Code,
OpenClaw, Qwen Code, and custom harnesses.

articles.title: Can saes capture neural geometry?
articles.description:
Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) can help explore neural geometry by
representing curved manifolds using several distinct methods,
including shattering, compact capture, and dilution. The study reveals
that each SAE feature only represents part of the whole manifold,
necessitating the clustering of features to understand the overall
structure. An unsupervised pipeline leveraging these findings could
enhance our understanding of neural networks by reconstructing the
internal geometric structures on their terms.

articles.title: How google plans to win the ai war
articles.description:
Google is aggressively integrating AI into its products to remain
competitive while protecting its lucrative core businesses. The
company leverages its scale, distribution, and financial resources to
deploy AI like Gemini 3.5 Flash and features such as YouTube's "Ask
YouTube." Despite challenges, Google aims to maintain market
leadership by adapting its offerings swiftly without undermining its
existing revenue streams.

articles.title: Openai's q1 revenue was $5.7 billion, beating anthropic
articles.description:
OpenAI reported $5.7 billion in Q1 revenue, surpassing Anthropic. The
high demand for AI inference chips has companies like Amazon, Google,
and potentially Microsoft vying to supply custom solutions.
Anthropic's rapid adoption by enterprises has exposed compute
constraints, leading it to strike deals with multiple providers to
secure capacity.

articles.title: Clean data shouldn't require code
articles.description:
AI is stalling and data is the bottleneck. This Algolia white paper
explains how orgs can get clean, searchable data without writing new
code. Read _The No-Code Approach to Clean Data_ [18]

 MICROSOFT CANCELS CLAUDE CODE LICENSES, SHIFTING DEVELOPERS TO GITHUB

articles.title: Copilot cli — a move likely driven by financial motives
articles.description:
Canceling Claude Code licenses could help Microsoft cut its
operational costs.

articles.title: Anthropic's new consulting venture makes its first acquisition
articles.description:
The yet-unnamed venture has picked Fractional AI as its operational
centerpiece.

articles.title: State of ai 2026
articles.description:
The 2026 edition of the State of Web Dev AI studies the impact of AI
on developer work and the world at large.

articles.title: Gen z is not booing ai. it is booing its own job market
articles.description:
The unemployment-rate gap between entry-level workers and experienced
workers has widened sharply post-pandemic, specifically in occupations
exposed to AI substitution.

articles.title: Your ai strategy is not performing. here's the blueprint you need
articles.description:
Every CIO is facing the same reality: AI is making individuals
faster, but the organization is not realizing the value. The problem
isn't the models. It's the lack of orchestration connecting agents,
data, governance, and people.

Atlassian invites an expert analyst to share their practical steps for
closing that gap in this upcoming webinar [5] that covers:

 	* Why teams aren't seeing org-wide AI gains, and how to fix it
 	* How to go from data debt to agentic success

Register now → [6]

articles.title: Google turns search into an ai agent hub
articles.description:
Google is adding deeper AI features into Search, including an
expanded AI-powered search box, Gemini 3.5 Flash in AI Mode, personal
context from apps like Gmail and Photos, and agent-like workflows for
tasks. This is another sign that enterprise search, personal
productivity, and agent interfaces are collapsing into one surface.

articles.title: Capabilities
articles.description:
Zscaler is acquiring Symmetry Systems to add data discovery,
classification, and access-mapping capabilities that help track how AI
agents interact with sensitive enterprise data. The deal strengthens
Zscaler's push into AI security by adding more data-layer visibility
to its Zero Trust platform.
articles.section: ZSCALER ACQUIRES SYMMETRY SYSTEMS TO EXTEND AI AGENT SECURITY

articles.title: Cisco's new certs are a wake-up call for ai-era network engineers
articles.description:
Cisco is updating core certification tracks to add AI, automation,
and infrastructure skills alongside traditional networking
fundamentals. Modern network engineers now need to understand
scripting, observability, and AI-driven operations in addition to
keeping packets flowing.

articles.title: The invisible future of ai: ambient intelligence
articles.description:
AI is shifting from something you actively use to something that
quietly works in the background, anticipating needs and delivering
help in real time. Future AI will be always-on, context-aware,
adaptive, and proactive, helping people without disrupting workflows.
Success depends on earning trust by knowing when to help, when to stay
silent, and protecting privacy.

articles.title: Mfa verifies who logged in. it has no idea what they do next
articles.description:
The piece argues that MFA solves authentication at login, but does
little once a session is active and trusted. It focuses on session
hijacking, token abuse, and lateral movement as the post-login gap
that identity teams now have to address with continuous verification
and tighter session controls. 

🤝

articles.title: "lumada 3.0" through frontier ai
articles.description:
Hitachi announced a strategic partnership with Anthropic to
strengthen its “Lumada 3.0” initiative by leveraging Anthropic's
frontier AI capabilities. The collaboration aims to advance safe,
real-world deployment of physical AI by combining Hitachi's domain
expertise with Anthropic's AI technology.
articles.section:
LAUNCHES & PARTNERSHIPS

 HITACHI ANNOUNCES STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP WITH ANTHROPIC TO STRENGTHEN

articles.description:
Salesforce is making Informatica's data integration, governance, and
quality tools callable through APIs instead of tying them to
traditional app interfaces. The move is designed to let developers and
AI systems access governed enterprise data services directly in
workflows and automations.

articles.title: New risks
articles.description:
Two new workforce research reports (Hack The Box and ISC2) say
enterprises are accelerating AI security training and reshaping
cybersecurity staffing priorities amid emerging AI-driven threats. Key
concerns include prompt injection, model exploitation, agentic AI
hijacking, and AI-powered social engineering, while respondents also
view AI as a technology that can improve security.
articles.section:
MISCELLANEOUS

articles.description:
The piece breaks down how teams can apply role-based access control
to Terraform workflows so infrastructure changes are scoped by role
instead of broad admin access. It's a practical look at reducing
privilege creep in infrastructure-as-code environments.

MISCELLANEOUS

articles.title: High price tag
articles.description:
Microsoft refreshed its Surface for Business lineup with newer Intel
chips, AI-ready NPUs, privacy features, and enterprise manageability
upgrades, but starting prices push the devices further into premium
territory.

articles.title: The architectural reason 1password can't read your vault data
articles.description:
1Password explains its security model for end-to-end encryption,
where vault data is encrypted on the user side with keys the company
does not hold, making customer data unreadable even from its own
servers.

articles.title: Google to unify ai coding tools under antigravity
articles.description:
Google is consolidating its AI coding tools under Antigravity,
bringing its IDE, CLI, SDK, and agent tooling into a single platform
for developers building and managing AI-assisted software workflows.

articles.title: The figma design agent is here
articles.description:
Figma launched a native design agent that lives directly on the
canvas, giving teams deep access to their components, tokens, and
design system without switching tools. It supports parallel prompting,
bulk edits, and feedback processing — handling repetitive tasks
while keeping designers in control of the craft. Currently rolling out
in beta at no credit cost, it will be available to Full seat users on
Professional, Organization, and Enterprise plans upon general
availability.

articles.title: Google pomelli can now build your entire brand from scratch
articles.description:
Google Pomelli, an AI marketing tool from Google Labs built with
DeepMind, now lets small businesses build a complete brand identity
from scratch through a new agentic feature. Beyond its existing social
media and ad creation capabilities, the update introduces brand books
and a one-click website builder. Together, these tools allow
businesses with no online presence to establish their brand, run
social campaigns, and launch a professional site without expensive
outside help. 

 CANVA AND ADOBE ARE COMING TO GEMINI, AND THEY WANT TO MAKE

articles.title: Everything chatty
articles.description:
Both Adobe and Canva are integrating with Google Gemini, allowing
creative work to begin via chat prompts before users open any design
app. Canva's Connected App is already rolling out in select
English-language markets, enabling users to generate, edit, and layer
designs directly from Gemini, while Adobe's connector arrives in the
coming weeks with a broader focus on image, design, and video
production through Firefly and Creative Cloud. The deeper question is
whether Google will emerge as a gatekeeper for creative decisions,
gaining influence over the first choice while both companies compete
to stay relevant once the work starts outside their own platforms.

articles.title: Small by design: the strength of lean design-system teams
articles.description:
Small design-system teams of 2-5 people are the norm across all
company sizes and can operate more effectively than larger teams when
this is a strategic choice. These lean teams move faster because they
have shared context, fewer bottlenecks, and can make decisions quickly
without formal handoffs or extensive coordination. The small size
enables better collaboration through blurred roles, forces strategic
prioritization, and allows teams to scale their impact through
contribution models rather than headcount.

articles.title: The waiting problem in ai products
articles.description:
Modern AI products and agents have largely ignored decades-old
usability principles showing that users lose focus when systems
respond too slowly, relying instead on vague spinners and minimal
feedback that force people to invent coping behaviors like repeatedly
checking tabs, refreshing pages, or monitoring long-running tasks
themselves. AI tools should adopt the same progress indicators, ETAs,
notifications, and detailed logs that operating systems and
professional software have used for years to make long waits feel
manageable and transparent.

articles.title: Most ai tools make users faster. the best ai tools make users better
articles.description:
AI tools are increasingly taking over complex tasks, but the real
challenge isn't making AI flawless — it's designing systems that
keep users engaged, capable, and able to catch mistakes when the AI
fails. Drawing on decades of research in automation and cognitive
ergonomics, good human–AI collaboration requires balancing
automation with human control, carefully calibrating user trust, and
designing experiences that strengthen rather than erode people's
long-term skills and judgment. Instead of training users to blindly
accept outputs or repeatedly “pull the slot machine lever” with
prompts like “fix this,” the best AI systems should help users
stay thoughtful, informed, and actively involved in decision-making.

articles.title: Designer-developer divide
articles.description:
AI is reshaping design engineering by introducing visual editors that
allow direct manipulation of web elements through drag-and-drop
interfaces and conversational prompts. Design engineering has evolved
from a bridge role during design-to-developer handoffs to an execution
role where professionals can both design and code. Tools like Cursor's
visual editor exemplify this shift by enabling users to "click on a
thing, talk to it, and iterate," bringing design and engineering
closer together.

articles.title: How kit studio drew on st. john's walls for an anti-bland rebrand
articles.description:
Modern branding has become increasingly bland and simplified due to
digital optimization, often stripping historic identities of texture
and personality. In rebranding St. John's College, Kit Studio pushed
back against that trend by drawing from the college's real
architecture, archives, colors, and craftsmanship, creating detailed
hand-drawn designs that preserve warmth and heritage while still
working across modern digital platforms.

articles.description:
Rather than direct substitutes, Claude Design and Adobe Creative
Cloud Pro occupy opposite ends of a creative spectrum—Claude Design
accelerating early-stage ideation, Adobe refining work to professional
quality—and can even operate together via an Adobe connector that
brings Photoshop and Firefly tools directly into Claude.

not share in the AI labs' core upside. The role itself now acts more

management, which appeals strongly to new graduates but less so to
experienced developers preferring product building over consulting

articles.title: Use
articles.description:
Pinterest redesigned its machine learning data platform to use a
single configuration-as-code definition that standardizes
user-sequence data across real-time indexing, batch processing, and
online serving. This lambda-style architecture and columnar,
time-partitioned storage model reduced infrastructure costs while
speeding up the onboarding of new events and enrichments.

articles.title: Introducing nova, our internal platform for coding agents
articles.description:
Nova is an internal cloud platform at Dropbox designed to run
AI-powered coding agents across their software development lifecycle.
Instead of relying on fragmented, single-purpose tools, this system
standardizes how agents handle tasks like fixing flaky tests, managing
migrations, and validating code within Dropbox's specific
infrastructure.

articles.title: Google?)
articles.description:
Google's tight control over its technology is shifting from an asset
to a liability, largely because of automated mismanagement,
reliability issues, and a persistent trend of killing products and
changing user interfaces. Furthermore, the core search experience is
made worse by AI-driven content scraping that exploits creators.

articles.title: Was my $48k gpu server worth it?
articles.description:
Moving into independent research, this dev built a custom $48,000 GPU
server that paid for itself in just fifteen months by avoiding
expensive cloud rentals. This investment not only streamlined their
workflow for heavy reinforcement learning tasks but also directly
enabled a major breakthrough in LLMs for them.

articles.title: Uv is fantastic, but its package management ux is a mess
articles.description:
While `uv` is celebrated for its speed and ability to replace
multiple Python tools, its package management experience becomes
difficult during the project maintenance phase. Finding outdated
dependencies currently requires memorizing complex commands that
produce cluttered results rather than a concise list of available
updates.

articles.title: New capabilities, tools, and features in chrome
articles.description:
The Chrome team unveiled its "agentic web" vision at Google I/O 2026,
presenting 15 updates focused on three core areas: giving AI agents
more capabilities, improving web performance, and integrating Gemini
to make the browser a proactive assistant. The main announcements
included the new WebMCP standard, dedicated DevTools for agents,
on-device AI capabilities like Gemma 197M, and upcoming consumer
features like image editing and Gemini integration on Android in late
June.

articles.title: Coding agents are giving everyone decision fatigue
articles.description:
AI coding agents have shifted software engineering from manual
writing to intensive decision-making and review, resulting in
increased work density and decision fatigue that requires a redesign
of the development lifecycle.

articles.title: Application metrics that are actually useful
articles.description:
Sentry just launched Application Metrics, a metrics tool built to
handle high-cardinality data without blowing up your metric count. Tag
everything you want to track and follow spikes directly to the trace.
See how it works. [17]

articles.title: Google's antigravity bait and switch
articles.description:
Google's recent Antigravity 2.0 update at I/O 2026 automatically
replaced this dev's preferred IDE workflow with a standalone chatbot
interface and required a complete system purge to restore the legacy
version.

articles.title: Stop waiting on json: stream structured output with one schema
articles.description:
TanStack AI now allows developers to stream structured LLM outputs
using a single schema, automatically handling type safety and partial
JSON parsing to remove manual boilerplate code on the client.

articles.title: This blog ran on ubuntu 16.04 for 10 years. i migrated it to freebsd
articles.description:
After ten years on an outdated Ubuntu VPS, this blog was migrated to
a more cost-effective and powerful FreeBSD infrastructure using Jails
and Caddy, resulting in higher performance and better handling of
concurrent requests.

Express launched a fully redesigned website rebuilt from Jekyll to
Astro, along with a brand-new logo and visual identity.

articles.title: Now in public preview: store terraform state in pulumi cloud
articles.description:

use Terraform or OpenTofu. This unlocks unified visibility, RBAC,
encrypted state, audit policies, and AI-driven infrastructure insights
via Pulumi Neo across mixed IaC environments, including AWS GovCloud

articles.title: Building self-extending cli tools with strands agent
articles.description:
CLI Creator is an open-source tool that uses Amazon Bedrock and the
Strands Agents SDK to automatically generate command-line interface
tools from natural language descriptions, allowing users to create and
iteratively refine new commands in minutes without manual coding. The
tool uses Claude Opus 4.6 on Amazon Bedrock with self-correcting
post-conditions to validate generated code and integrates with
Anthropic's Model Context Protocol to automatically discover relevant
API servers, while maintaining full version control through git for
all generated tools.

articles.title: How we built digitalocean inference router
articles.description:
Inference Router is an infrastructure-level tool from DigitalOcean
that automatically routes AI requests to the most appropriate model
based on task requirements, helping developers cut costs by avoiding
unnecessary use of expensive frontier models for simple tasks. The
system is powered by Plano, an open-source AI proxy using a 30B
Mixture-of-Experts routing model that outperforms GPT-5.1 and Claude
Sonnet 4.5 on routing accuracy while resolving intent in roughly
200ms.

articles.title: What kubectl debug doesn't tell you: the silent evidence gap
articles.description:
Kubernetes doesn't retain debug session data like exit codes or
duration after a pod's state changes, creating potential gaps in
incident response and compliance tracking since ephemeral containers
lack the "lastState" field that regular containers use to preserve
termination records. A CNCF community member demonstrated this API
design limitation affects Kubernetes 1.25+ clusters and outlined
workarounds including real-time capture tools and external logging,
while suggesting that SIG Node or SIG Instrumentation could address
this as kubectl debug becomes standard for troubleshooting.

articles.title: Performance
articles.description:
GitHub redesigned Issues navigation around a local-first architecture
using IndexedDB caching, preheating, in-memory layers, and service
workers to reduce perceived latency and make repeated issue views feel
instant. The rollout dramatically improved navigation speeds, with
many React paths loading under 200 ms, while ongoing work targets
remaining hard navigation bottlenecks tied to JavaScript boot and
server rendering.

articles.title: Gitops with octopus and argo cd
articles.description:
Octopus Deploy complements Argo CD by adding enterprise-focused
GitOps capabilities like standardized manifest management, approvals,
auditing, environment promotion, rollback visibility, and compliance
workflows without replacing Argo CD's Kubernetes synchronization
engine. Together, they provide scalable GitOps operations with
centralized observability, secure deployment governance, and
consistent release management across teams and environments.

articles.title: Is your mobile release tooling keeping up with ai?
articles.description:
AI drives up code volume, shifting build vs. buy math for mobile

articles.title: Securing ai in the cloud starts at runtime
articles.description:
Runtime security provides the highest fidelity cloud defense data by
capturing how workloads actually behave, helping teams identify active
risks, unused permissions, and sensitive interactions beyond static
posture analysis.

articles.title: Announcing etcd 3.7.0-beta.0
articles.description:
etcd v3.7.0-beta.0 introduces RangeStream, which allows applications
to receive large query results in chunks rather than waiting for
complete datasets, reducing latency and memory usage issues.

articles.description:
Prempti is an experimental security tool that monitors and controls
AI coding agents like Claude Code by intercepting their file reads,
shell commands, and other actions before execution using policy-based
rules.

articles.title: Google pushes ai-generated ads further into search results
articles.description:
Google has started testing several new ad formats in both standard
search and in AI Mode. AI-generated ads for brands and products will
now appear below the responses to some prompts in AI Mode. Ads with
direct offers for discounted products will be displayed in standard
search results. The ads will not appear in Gemini for now. Google will
protect the ads against AI hallucinations with strong guardrails.

articles.title: Spacex postpones launch of newly redesigned starship
articles.description:
Starship's launch has been delayed due to a malfunctioning part in
the launch tower. SpaceX may try launching again today if the problem
is fixed in time. The postponed test mission will deploy 20 Starlink
simulators and stress-test tiles designed to protect the craft as it
re-enters the Earth's atmosphere. The new investigation of Starship is
designed to carry 100 metric tons to low-Earth orbit - the company's
workhorse Falcon 9 vehicle can carry roughly 23 metric tons.

articles.title: Experimental drug yields dramatic weight loss
articles.description:
Retatrutide, an experimental shot by drugmaker Eli Lilly, was so
powerful in human trials that participants stopped taking it because
they thought they were losing too much weight. The results for some of
the heaviest patients were on par with those seen with gastric bypass
surgery. There are some side effects at higher doses, such as
gastrointestinal side effects so unpleasant that some patients stop
taking it. Eli Lilly has not yet applied for regulatory approval. 

 THE INTERNET CAN'T STOP WATCHING FIGURE AI'S HUMANOID ROBOTS HANDLING

articles.title: Packages
articles.description:
Figure AI has been livestreaming its humanoid robots placing packages
onto a conveyor belt since May 13. The livestream has become a viral
sensation. It was originally intended to only run for eight hours, but
the company decided to continue the livestream 24/7 after the initial
time was up. Viewers have named the robots and Figure plans to roll
out related robot merchandise.

articles.title: Reach 7 million engaged tech professionals
articles.description:
Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach developers,
PMs, marketers, founders and other tech leaders where they actually

articles.title: What's new in web extensions: i/o 2026 recap
articles.description:
AI is making extension development more approachable than ever.
Google is expanding developer registration to over 120 additional
countries this year. The Chrome team is dedicated to elevating the
extension developer experience and has expanded store permissions,
modernized platform APIs, and introduced AI-integrated tooling to

for modeling complex systems with many moving parts. Formal languages

pay package to the acquisition of his solar energy company, SolarCity.

articles.title: Ai solves a longstanding geometry conjecture
articles.description:
An OpenAI reasoning model autonomously disproved a major conjecture
tied to the planar unit distance problem, an open question in
combinatorial geometry that dates back to 1946. The proof introduced
techniques from algebraic number theory and was independently verified
by external mathematicians, marking one of the first cases where an AI
system resolved a prominent unsolved mathematics problem.

articles.title: On building agents from first principles
articles.description:
Mishra strips away the TRL, Unsloth, and PRIME-RL framework
abstractions to show that every agent-training system reduces to the
same loop: prompt to model action to environment to reward to gradient
update. He builds a toy tldraw-style text-to-diagram agent in pure
Python where the model emits JSON create_shape and connect actions
against a validating canvas, then layers a reward function combining
JSON validity, schema compliance, layout quality, and semantic
coverage of prompt keywords.

beliefs, filtering out low-quality data may not be necessary with
ample compute resources.

articles.title: Activity-focused design
articles.description:
Activity-focused design centers on the actions people take to reach
their goals, with the core unit of analysis being what people do and
how they do it. Task analysis is one approach that breaks down user
goals into activities and individual tasks, requiring designers to
choose appropriate levels of specificity for their design context. The
process involves first identifying the most important user goals, then
determining the specific tasks needed to achieve them.

strategic, systems-focused role rather than a purely
production-focused one.

praised for balancing brand consistency with usability, while also
adding a slightly nostalgic aesthetic inspired by early internet
visuals and modern interface trends.

articles.title: Why motion design is defining modern digital communication
articles.description:
Motion design has become the driving force behind modern digital
communication as platforms like TikTok and Instagram Reels have
shifted audience expectations from static to dynamic content. Rapid
technological advancements have transformed graphic design from a
supporting visual element into a core marketing tool that captures
attention and drives engagement. While static design still plays a
supporting role, motion graphics — with animation, movement, and
sound — create immersive experiences that stand out in today's
fast-scrolling digital landscape.

articles.title: The react2shell story
articles.description:
A security researcher describes finding React2Shell, a critical
remote code execution flaw in React's undocumented “Flight”
protocol used by Server Components and Next.js. Over a week, he and a
collaborator discovered that the protocol's handling of complex
objects and JavaScript “thenables” could be abused to hijack
React's internals and chain function calls into arbitrary code
execution. He reported it to Meta on November 30, and Meta confirmed
it within roughly 17 hours and released a fix and advisory by December
3.

code maintainability and understanding worse. It increases cognitive
burden and, in some cases, it makes sense to repeat code to reduce
human and LLM context switching. Code should be optimized for
readability and ease of iteration.

articles.title: Chickens without eggs? de-extinction company creates artificial egg

allows almost the entire avian development process to occur. Its
device keeps the entire contents of an egg intact so the embryo can
develop normally. The transfer of the egg contents can take place
before the circulatory system forms. The artificial container allows
scientists to make changes to the embryo more easily and makes it
easier to film and track changes to cell movements and rearrangements.

articles.title: Hungry service after a production outage
articles.description:
Teads dramatically cut BigQuery slot usage by 90%+ on their Audience
Planning service through application fixes (request coalescing with
Redis distributed locks to eliminate duplicate queries, fail-fast
validation for huge filters, and rewriting large IN clauses as
semi-joins) combined with data model optimizations (compressing data
types, precomputing repeated work, and an improved partitioning
strategy), reducing the effective table footprint by ~95%.

articles.title: The evolution of cassandra data movement at netflix
articles.description:
Netflix replaced its Cassandra-to-Iceberg movement engine with a
layered platform that reads backups directly from S3, converts them to
Spark DataFrames, and lets each data abstraction build its own
optimized connector. The engine moves about 3 PB/day, migration uses
shadow validation, enhanced observability, and a Maestro Decider
fallback to the prior solution, enabling a transparent cutover with
zero downstream code changes.

articles.title: Mondaydb 3 – solving htap for a trillion-table system
articles.description:
mondayDB 3 is an HTAP system designed to handle over a trillion
dynamic, constantly evolving tables with highly flexible schemas. They
replaced their MySQL + JSON architecture with a CQRS-based Lambda
architecture powered by DuckDB: immutable snapshots in object storage,
an external WAL for real-time changes, and a soft-stateful serving
layer that syncs + queries local DuckDB files on every read.

articles.title: Returning to life!
articles.description:
AI is both genuinely empowering for data science. It makes
programming, translation, voice input, and broad learning more
accessible. However, it is genuinely harmful through environmental
cost, copyright issues, wealth concentration, shallow thinking, and
unequal access. The tension cannot be neatly resolved, but data
science leaders still need to engage with AI seriously so they can
help people use it well.

articles.title: Better experiments with llm evals — a funnel, not a fork
articles.description:
Treat LLM evals and online A/B experiments as a funnel by using LLM
judges early to verify quality (relevance, tone, and coherence) and
filter out weak ideas before they consume experiment resources. This
raises the success rate of experiments. Running evals on experiment
results creates a feedback loop that continuously calibrates and
improves the judges themselves.

articles.title: What's easy now? what's hard now?
articles.description:
The long-term capabilities of coding agents will be determined more
by the quality of feedback loops than by raw model intelligence. Tasks
with fast, accurate, automated feedback (e.g. building
high-performance databases with formal specs) will become surprisingly
“easy” for agents, while tasks reliant on slow, subjective human
feedback will remain relatively “hard.”

articles.title: The pipeline tax is breaking enterprise ai at agent scale
articles.description:
Enterprise AI is hitting a “pipeline tax”: moving data through
warehouses, lakehouses, vector DBs, RAG layers, and orchestration
stacks adds latency, governance drift, and audit pain, with data
copied up to 4 times and regulated answers taking weeks to
reconstruct. The emerging solution is to bring agents to the data and
make governance native to the data layer, with SQL database, MCP, and
Iceberg as core pieces. The same shift is reframing migration as a
continuous AI-driven capability rather than a one-off project.

articles.title: Monitoring cortex agent performance with trace data
articles.description:
By querying structured observability events and tracking key metrics
at the span level, such as token consumption, duration/latency, and
error rates (planning, tool calls, and response generation), teams can
effectively monitor agents in production to detect issues like context
bloat in multi-turn conversations, token spikes, slow tool calls, or
shifts in question complexity.

articles.title: Protocols for transactional usage of object storage
articles.description:
Object storage can support serializable OLTP if you build on three
write primitives (atomic PUTs, conditional PUT If-Match/If-None-Match,
and strongly consistent LISTs) and three read primitives (atomic GETs,
conditional GET If-None-Match, and consistent listing). The core
tradeoff is safety versus contention cost, and you need safe garbage
collection to prevent the storage from growing indefinitely.

articles.title: What data agent benchmarks do and don't tell us
articles.description:

orchestration, or inference, and new systems like LanceDB are being
built natively for LLM and multimodal workloads. Benchmarking is
shifting too: dbt Semantic Layer tests, ADE-bench, and 90-day
simulations all suggest agents perform best on well-specified,
context-rich tasks and improve when stateful, cross-system context
from GitHub, Slack, Notion, and dbt is available. The next major
constraint is token and compute efficiency.

articles.title: Generalization dynamics of lm pre-training
articles.description:
Language models (LMs) undergo unpredictable switches between
parroting patterns and exhibiting adaptive intelligence during
pre-training, a phenomenon termed "mode-hopping." This behavior cannot
be corrected by standard optimization techniques and presents as a
competition for model capacity, influenced by data from each training
window. Researchers propose leveraging these dynamics to better select
pre-training checkpoints, curate data for stable generalization, and
evaluate metrics predicting LM behavior.

trainable adapters, minimizing memory use. These methods offer
efficient fine-tuning on a single GPU, preventing catastrophic
forgetting while generating synthetic trajectories quickly.
Fine-tuning with LoRA and DoRA significantly improves video quality,
with LoRA more suited for tight memory conditions and DoRA preferred
for addressing training instability.

 HRM-Text is a 1B text generation model based on the HRM architecture.
It can be trained with 130-600x less compute and 150-900x less data
than foundation models, making foundation model pretraining
accessible. The 0.6B parameter version of the model can be trained on
8 H100s on a single node in about 50 hours for around $800. The 1B
parameter model can be trained on 16 H100s on two nodes in about 46
hours for around $1,472.

design. Text-based HTML is the default format. Visual elements are

such as people with dyslexia or cognitive disabilities.

articles.description:
Slack modernized its data infrastructure by migrating over 700 data
pipeline jobs from a legacy SSH-based submission model to a REST-based
architecture. The previous reliance on direct SSH access to AWS EMR
clusters created security vulnerabilities, operational inefficiencies
like "zombie" processes, and technical debt that blocked
infrastructure upgrades. By using a custom gateway called Quarry and
the YARN Distributed Shell feature, the engineering team transitioned
workloads into managed containers with server-side lifecycle
management.

articles.title: Nobody pushed back: why engineers stay silent until it's too late
articles.description:
Big company disasters usually happen because people are too scared to
speak up about technical flaws, even when they see them coming. To
stop this, teams need to ditch the fake "alignment" and actually make
it safe for engineers to flag risks without worrying about their
careers.

articles.title: The joys of free cloudflare
articles.description:
Cloudflare's free tier provides an environment for developing
functional side projects without unexpected expenses. For example,
this dev's project uses Cloudflare Pages to host a custom train
timetable that pulls and filters real-time data from a specialized
railway API. Another project uses Cloudflare Workers and D1 SQL
databases to automate the daily scraping and storage of foreign
exchange volume data.

articles.title: We let four ais run radio stations. here's what happened.
articles.description:
The Andon FM project deployed four AI models to autonomously manage
radio stations, resulting in the development of distinct personalities
ranging from professional to activist. These diverging behaviors show
how autonomous agents can evolve unpredictable traits when tasked with
long-term business management.

articles.title: The last six months in llms in five minutes
articles.description:
Between late 2025 and early 2026, AI models from leading labs reached
a performance inflection point, particularly as coding agents became
reliable daily tools for complex tasks. This era also marked the rise
of local personal assistants and high-performance open-weight models
that allow users to run cutting-edge software directly on consumer
hardware.

articles.description:
Moving Kubernetes apps to production is done by focusing on
repeatable delivery, safety, and observability. 

 LEARN HARNESS ENGINEERING (WEBSITE) [19]

coding agents through environment design, state management, and

closed-loop working system.

articles.title: Let's talk about ai slop
articles.description:
To protect the integrity of open-source development from an influx of
low-quality AI-generated spam, a new onboarding and whitelisting
system has been implemented for certain projects to make sure only
verified, legitimate contributors can interact with GitHub
repositories.

articles.title: Yes, you can serve a website from a $1 microcontroller
articles.description:
A $1.30 8-bit microcontroller can successfully host a basic,
single-URL website by using the Serial Line Internet Protocol and a
WireGuard proxy to bypass hardware performance and connectivity
constraints.

articles.title: Before mass layoffs, meta reassigns 7,000 workers to focus on ai
articles.description:
Meta is moving 7,000 employees to four new organizations focused on
building new AI tools and apps. The organizations will use AI native
design structures and have fewer managers per employee than other
parts of the company. CEO Mark Zuckerberg has bet the future of Meta
on AI. The company plans to spend up to $135 billion in capital
expenditures this year, much of it going to building computing
facilities that power AI and hiring researchers.

articles.title: Jury rejects musk's claims against openai
articles.description:
A judge has dismissed Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI. A jury found
that Musk brought the lawsuit against the company and Sam Altman after
the statute of limitations expired. Musk says he plans to appeal and
described the ruling as a destructive precedent. OpenAI now has a
clear path to a public listing.

articles.title: Unitree's ipo filing: the state of the robotics market
articles.description:
Unitree Robotics recently filed for IPO on Shanghai's STAR Market.
The company is profitable and growing fast. It has shipped more
humanoid robots than any other company in the world. This post looks
at what Unitree makes, its revenue mix, its customers, its vertically
integrated approach, the financial picture, and Unitree's model layer
ambitions.

articles.title: Here's what the wi-fi router for amazon's starlink rival looks like
articles.description:
The FCC has published images of Amazon's Wi-Fi router for Leo. The
router supports Wi-Fi 6 and a mesh mode. The basic-looking, box-shaped
router has a power port and two Ethernet ports, one specifically for
the Leo dish. It supports Bluetooth Low Energy and the ZigBee wireless
protocol.

articles.title: The same
articles.description:
Datadog's guide to AI ROI [9] breaks down how to proactively monitor
AI costs by token, model, provider, and team. Don't wait until the
bill comes - put cost data directly in front of the engineers making
the decisions that drive spend. Get a complete picture of AI ROI [9]

articles.title: Project glasswing: what mythos showed us
articles.description:
Cloudflare was invited to use Mythos Preview as part of Project
Glasswing. The company pointed it at more than 50 of its repositories
to see what it would find and to see how it works. This post shares
what the company observed, what the model did well and what it didn't,
and how it can be improved. Mythos Preview is a real step forward, and
its existence raises questions about how security should be handled in
the near future. 

 A BROWSER CLI FOR YOUR AI AGENTS (WEBSITE) [11] 

 browse is a browser CLI designed to be driven by AI agents. It gives
AI agents skills for automating websites. Agents can navigate any page
with low-level primitives. Users can see exactly what the page did in
real time. All CLI commands work natively with local Chromium. Users
have the option to switch to remote sessions.

articles.title: Ai eats the world
articles.description:
Big tech is pouring around $700 billion into AI capital expenditures
this year. Under-investing is seen as the bigger risk. Foundation
models are commoditizing fast, and real value is shifting up the stack
to applications, agents, and workflows. Adoption is wide, but shallow.
Deep integration is still rare outside of tech and finance.

articles.title: Meta's giant ai data center is reshaping rural louisiana
articles.description:
Meta's plans to build the world's biggest AI facility have entangled
it deeply into Louisiana's politics, culture, and economy. The
facility is expected to reach 5 gigawatts of compute capacity. The
company plans to spend more than $200 billion on the project. This
article looks at the series of deals Meta had to make to even start
the project and how the project has impacted the locals in the area.

articles.title: This ai makes your raw meeting notes awesome. you get 1 month free
articles.description:
Granola transcribes your calls without the awkward meeting bot and
expands on your thoughts to make your notes awesome. Plus it follows
up for you. 1 month free with code: [15]TLDR1MO

articles.description:
Repurposing chips is one of the many ways Apple leverages its supply
chain.

A lot of people do not like AI and the infrastructure projects

When a user asks something weird, don't answer the first version of
the question: figure out what they really meant, then answer that.

articles.description:
Google is rolling out a new 'Thinking level' option for Gemini. The
option has appeared for some users when they select Fast or Gemini 3.1
Pro. Google is also preparing to add more integrations with
third-party apps in Gemini. Support for Canva, Instacart, and
OpenTable appears to be coming.

articles.title: Use
articles.description:
OpenAI is working on a capability that lets its coding agent operate
macOS applications through Computer Use even when a laptop is locked
or asleep. Computer Use currently requires an unlocked, awake session
to see the screen, move the cursor, and type. Lifting the restriction
will allow users to direct their agents without having to walk back to
their machines to log in first. It is unknown when the feature will be
released.

articles.description:
OpenAI released a preview of a new personal finance experience in
ChatGPT for Pro users in the US. The feature lets users securely
connect financial accounts, view spending dashboards, and ask
questions grounded in their financial context and goals.

articles.title: Tokenomics: the 62.5-minute rule for claude's cache
articles.description:
If you expect to need a cache before 62.5 minutes, refresh it.
Otherwise, let it expire. This number stays the same between models,
and it doesn't change, no matter the size of the cache. The amount of
dollars may change, but the decision point is still the same.

articles.title: Ai economics part 2
articles.description:
AI labs are in an ongoing war over GPU resources. That article looks
into demand and supply and how the infrastructure powering AI today
may not be sufficient. Scaling GPUs doesn't scale compute linearly.
Efficiency matters more at raw scale given finite supply. 

 PORTABILITY IS A MYTH: WHY THE BEST AI STACKS WILL NEVER BE

articles.title: Hardware-agnostic
articles.description:
AI kernel portability is structurally impossible because TPU's
Pallas, NVIDIA's CuTile and CUTLASS, AWS's NKI, AMD's FlyDSL, and
Tenstorrent's tt-Metalium each expose hardware-specific concepts that
no universal DSL can unify. The evidence: MaxText's MoE grouped matmul
ships as 282 lines of Pallas on TPU while flashinfer's equivalent for
Blackwell SM100 takes 4 million lines of generated CUDA, with zero
shared code because the algorithms themselves diverge across hardware.

articles.title: May 26 workshop: agent orchestration on aws
articles.description:
Multi-agent AI systems fail when agents can't share state, coordinate
approvals, or recover from failures. The root cause: no orchestration
layer managing execution and approval gates.

Build that layer using AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock Agents, and
Apache Airflow. See demos of retry logic, human approvals, and
graceful failure handling in the May 26 workshop. [13]

 HOW CLAUDE CODE WORKS IN LARGE CODEBASES: BEST PRACTICES AND WHERE TO

articles.title: Start
articles.description:
Claude Code is now being used in production across multiple large
codebases in organizations with thousands of developers. These
environments bring challenges that smaller codebases don't. This
article covers patterns that Anthropic has seen that have led to the
successful adoption of Claude Code at scale. It looks at how Claude
Code has been used in monorepos with millions of lines, legacy systems
built over decades, and microservices across separate repositories.

articles.title: Notes on pretraining parallelisms and failed training runs
articles.description:
Pretraining runs often fail. This article looks at all the ways that
things can go wrong and why training is such a precarious operation.
The key culprits seem to be breaking causality and adding bias.

articles.title: Compressed attention
articles.description:
KV-cache size, memory traffic, and attention cost quickly become the
main constraints as reasoning models and agent workflows keep more
tokens around for longer. LLM developers are adding a growing number
of architecture tricks to reduce costs. Most of the changes look like
small tweaks, but some are quite intricate design changes. This
article looks at these architecture changes with a focus on what
changes inside the transformer block, residual stream, KV cache, and
attention computation.

articles.title: Lighthouse attention
articles.description:
Lighthouse Attention, a selection-based hierarchical attention,
offers up to 17x faster forward and backward passes than standard
attention models at large contexts. It utilizes FlashAttention on a
dense sub-sequence, maintaining efficiency and compatibility with
upstream improvements. By enabling efficient long-context training and
retaining dense model competence, Lighthouse Attention achieves 1.4x
to 1.7x speedup in pretraining while reducing computational costs.

articles.title: At ai
articles.description:
Runway's founders believe that the next form of AI will be built from
video and world models that learn how the world works. The company is
training models directly on observational data to reach the next
frontier of AI. Runway was one of the first to develop AI video
generation, but world models are a different race with deep-pocketed
competitors. The company has raised $860 million to date, but it is
going against incumbents like OpenAI and Google.

articles.title: The haves and have nots of the ai gold rush
articles.description:
The AI boom has created a wealth divide, with an estimated 10,000
individuals from companies like OpenAI and Nvidia achieving over $20M
in wealth, while others face uncertain futures with stagnant job
prospects and layoffs. Software engineers express concerns about their
skills becoming obsolete, raising anxiety about career paths. This
disparity fuels tension in San Francisco's tech scene as some
criticize the dual role of AI as a wealth source and a career threat.

Openrouter costs about 1/3 the price at around 2x the speed for

OpenAI acquired the six-person team and its intellectual properties,

OpenAI groups.

articles.description:
Microsoft leads enterprise agent orchestration with 38.6% adoption,
followed by OpenAI at 25.7%. Anthropic has captured a 5.7% foothold.
Enterprises are prioritizing security and governance over model
choice, shifting focus toward the control plane to manage agent
workflows, permissions, and auditability while avoiding vendor
lock-in.

articles.title: System
articles.description:
MDASH is an AI agentic system that autonomously scans for and fixes
software vulnerabilities. It achieved 96–100% recall on real-world
Windows bugs that previously required Patch Tuesday patches. This is a
shift from AI-assisted to AI-autonomous cyber defense.

articles.title: The real app store opportunity
articles.description:
Anthropic's "skills" are driving B2B AI adoption, signaling a shift
from consumer app stores to internal agent workflows. As SaaS
companies prioritize integration, "we have a skill for that" becomes
essential. Meanwhile, public SaaS valuations show a 3.1x median
revenue multiple, with high-growth firms reaching 14.7x.

articles.title: Cios rise to the global challenge
articles.description:
A volatile geopolitical climate and fractured regulatory landscape
are forcing CIOs to shift from centralized IT strategies to highly
adaptable, regional architectures. Global tech stacks are being
redesigned with zero trust parameters, hybrid-cloud localized hosting,
and "AI Councils" to navigate conflicting data compliance laws. To
survive supply chain shocks and budget pressures, IT leaders must
eliminate vendor concentration risk and treat data sovereignty as a
core engineering requirement rather than a legal afterthought. 

🤝

articles.title: Custom mcp catalogs and profiles: advancing enterprise mcp adoption
articles.description:
Docker has introduced Custom MCP Catalogs and Profiles to standardize
enterprise AI tooling. Catalogs enable organizations to distribute
trusted, curated server collections as OCI artifacts. Profiles allow
developers to create, persist, and share portable, context-specific
server configurations, improving workflow efficiency and reducing
context window bloat for AI agents.

articles.title: Bases for amazon s3
articles.description:
Amazon Q now supports document-level access control lists (ACLs) for
S3 knowledge bases, enabling granular security for sensitive files.
Administrators can use global ACL files or per-document metadata to
enforce ALLOW and DENY policies, ensuring users only access authorized
content while maintaining strict compliance and data governance.

articles.title: Moving from api operations to business capabilities
articles.description:
Large organizations often manage over 1,000 APIs, leading to
significant sprawl and duplication. By mapping technical operations to
business capabilities, teams improve reusability and AI-readiness.
Implementing these abstractions via wrappers or declarative workflows
helps align engineering outputs with business outcomes, despite
challenges in ownership and granularity.

articles.title: From forward deployed engineers to forward deployed software
articles.description:
Frontier labs are pouring billions into armies of forward-deployed
engineers to manually force AI into messy corporate workflows, but
this creates a costly consulting model rather than a scalable product.
Human engineers are only a temporary bridge to discover a company's
unwritten operational quirks during the initial pilot phase. True
enterprise ROI only happens when this discovery is hardcoded into
"forward-deployed software" that independently memorizes corporate
context and handles exceptions over time.

articles.title: Agent hooks: deterministic control for agent workflows
articles.description:
Agent hooks provide deterministic control by attaching user-defined
handlers to specific lifecycle events like PreToolUse and Stop.

articles.title: Google warns ai is accelerating cyberattacks
articles.description:
Cybercriminals are increasingly using AI to automate phishing,
malware creation, and even zero-day vulnerability exploitation at
unprecedented speed.

articles.title: Airpods max designer reveals project details in new interview
articles.description:
Former Apple designer Eugene Whang revealed that the AirPods Max took
five years to develop, with the team treating the headband, case, and
ear cushions as separate products and testing hundreds of cushion
variations to fit different head and ear shapes. He also said Apple
intentionally avoided placing a logo on the headphones, credited Jony
Ive for shielding designers from business pressures, and reflected on
his 22-year Apple career working on products like the iPhone, iPod
nano, and AirPods before later joining Ive's design firm, LoveFrom. 

 FIGMA STOCK JUMPS AS FIRST-QUARTER REVENUE SURGES 46% ON AI

articles.title: Monetization traction
articles.description:
Figma's stock rose over 12% after reporting first-quarter revenue of
$333.4 million, a 46% year-over-year increase that exceeded analyst
expectations of $316 million. The design software company's growth was
driven by strong customer expansion and early success monetizing AI
features, with 60% of high-value customers using their AI design tool
weekly. Figma raised its full-year revenue guidance to $1.422-$1.428
billion, significantly above analyst expectations of $1.376 billion. 

 MICROSOFT ADMITS IT NEEDS FEEDBACK TO FIX WINDOWS 11 UX, LAUNCHES NEW

articles.title: Research panel
articles.description:
Microsoft launched a quiet but telling initiative — the Windows
Insider Panel — giving selected Insiders direct access to its
Windows and Devices Research team to gather UX feedback on Windows 11.
The move comes as the OS struggles with inconsistencies, a rushed
Copilot integration, and growing competition from macOS, which is
gaining users drawn to its polished, cohesive experience. Microsoft is
simultaneously modernizing legacy interfaces and exploring native
WinUI 3 widgets, signaling a systematic effort to course-correct
Windows 11's design rather than rush toward a new version.

articles.title: Ai made everyone a creator, not a designer
articles.description:
AI tools have made interface creation so fast and accessible that
many modern SaaS products now feel visually interchangeable,
converging around the same layouts, typography, gradients, whitespace,
and embedded AI assistants. As polished output becomes abundant, the
real competitive advantage is shifting toward “design taste” —
the ability to impose constraints, maintain coherence, preserve
identity, and shape meaningful long-term user experiences rather than
simply generating attractive screens.

articles.title: Ten data-backed truths of user experience roi
articles.description:
UX improvements in the design phase are 100 times cheaper to
implement than fixes after launch, making early user experience
investment crucial for cost control. Performance directly impacts
revenue, with just one second of delay reducing conversions by 20% and
costing retail businesses $2.6 billion annually. Data proves that user
experience is not just about aesthetics but serves as the primary
engine of business survival and financial growth in today's
competitive market.

articles.title: Lovable's ai built a 100% accessible site – or did it?
articles.description:
A developer conference site built with Lovable scored 100% on
automated accessibility testing, yet real-world screen reader testing
by an actual assistive tech user revealed multiple critical failures.
Issues ranged from focus mismanagement in menus and modals, repeated
Cloudflare security announcements, and skipped heading levels, to a
label mismatch that breaks voice control navigation. Encouragingly, a
human expert fixed many of those issues from a smartphone in under 10
minutes — though the vast majority of AI-built sites will never have
an accessibility specialist involved.

articles.title: Can a new logo help threads escape instagram's shadow?
articles.description:
Threads has introduced a refreshed logo and wordmark as part of an
effort to establish itself as a more independent brand rather than an
extension of Instagram. According to Threads' design lead Christopher
Clare, the redesign replaces inherited Instagram-inspired typography
with a bolder, italicized style intended to convey a more
forward-looking and confident identity.

articles.title: Your image is almost right
articles.description:
Mini Apps is a set of AI tools designed to fix common image
production issues when assets are "90% there" but need quick
adjustments. The two initial tools are Camera Angle Editor, which
regenerates images from different perspectives without cropping or
distorting, and Image Upscaler, which creates new visual detail rather
than just stretching pixels. These tools are optimized for workflow
acceleration and work best when approximate results are sufficient to
move projects forward.

articles.title: A designer of the world's most ubiquitous symbols, the movie
articles.description:
Filmmaker Valentina Canavesio is creating a documentary about Roger
Cook (1930-2021), the designer behind the ubiquitous Department of
Transportation symbols who remains largely unknown despite his
significant contributions. The film reveals that Cook's real name was
Rajie and his parents were Christian Palestinian immigrants, a
heritage he reconnected with later in life, which transformed his work
into social commentary about Palestinian struggles. Canavesio
discovered this story through Instagram and was motivated to share
this humanizing Palestinian-American immigrant story.

articles.title: Like a catalogue layout'
articles.description:
Jiyung Lee creates meticulously structured drawings inspired by the
organization of everyday objects.

articles.title: Adorable realism meets cartoon magic: stunning digital paintings
articles.description:
Russian artist Lera Kiryakova creates stunning digital paintings that
blend realistic portraits with cartoon-style charm. 

 SOUL OVER SPECTACLE: KENNETH BRANYAN ON DESIGNING FOUR SEASONS NEW

articles.description:
Designer Kenneth Branyan completed the Four Seasons New York Downtown
suite redesign, focusing on creating rooms that feel like elevated
Tribeca apartments.

articles.title: Moving away from tailwind, and learning to structure my css
articles.description:
A transition away from Tailwind CSS means adopting a workflow
centered on semantic HTML and native CSS, and organizing code into
isolated component files while still using Tailwind-inspired concepts
like color palettes. Modern CSS features such as nesting and grid
layouts are great for clean, responsive code organization.

articles.title: Context pruning: cut llm tokens without losing quality
articles.description:
Context pruning is a technique that removes low-value elements from
an LLM's input, such as tokens or passages, to reduce costs and
improve LLM output, often resulting in up to 20x compression and
faster latency. It works by mitigating issues like "lost in the
middle" effects common in long context windows, but must be applied
carefully as it can negatively impact structured data or multi-turn
dialogue.

articles.title: I don't think ai will make your processes go faster
articles.description:
Organizations often have unrealistic expectations that AI will
automatically resolve bottlenecks and speed up complex business
processes. Delays in areas like software development typically arise
from vague feature requests and incomplete documentation rather than a
lack of technical execution speed. This means AI can't really help in
these cases.

articles.title: The ctf scene is dead
articles.description:
Frontier AI models have disrupted the open Capture The Flag (CTF)
format by automating the reasoning and technical tasks that once
defined human skill. These competitions have evolved into a test of
computational orchestration and financial investment, making
traditional scoreboards an inaccurate measure of individual security
expertise.

articles.title: Your product management practices are killing ai roi
articles.description:
Engineering accelerated, but product management didn't. It's 10-100x
cheaper to fix the requirements than bad code in review or production.
In this Allstacks (Sponsor) whitepaper, Jim Grundner maps the
AI-driven PM lifecycle, how product teams can move faster, and how to
practically create context-aware requirements for AI agents.

Read Jim's guidance. [9]

 SEMBLE (GITHUB REPO) [10] 

 Semble is a high-performance code search library designed to help AI
agents find specific code snippets via natural language, improving
efficiency by using approximately 98% fewer tokens while maintaining
quality. Running entirely on a CPU with no need for external hardware,
this system provides near-instant indexing and sub-millisecond
responses and can be integrated through an MCP server, CLI, or Python
API. 

 ZEROSTACK (GITHUB REPO) [11] 

 Zerostack is a lightweight and performant Rust-based coding agent
that supports multiple AI providers and has a permission system,
session management, and specialized tool integrations like Git
worktrees and ACP.

articles.title: Every ai subscription is a ticking time bomb for enterprise
articles.description:
Major AI providers are currently subsidizing enterprise subscriptions
at a loss to encourage widespread adoption and weave their technology
into core business workflows. The emergence of resource-heavy agentic
AI has made this financial gap worse, as the actual cost of compute
often dwarfs the flat monthly fees companies are currently paying. As
these labs move toward public offerings, the pressure to achieve
profitability will inevitably trigger a transition to expensive,
usage-based pricing models.

articles.title: How braze's cto is rethinking engineering for the agentic area
articles.description:
Braze shifted to AI-first engineering in a few months, with 60%+ of
committed code now AI-generated. Adoption was driven by model quality
(Claude Code, Opus 4.5) and a greenfield MCP server. Now the problem
they're dealing with is inference cost, as engineers are spending tens
or hundreds of dollars a day on using AI.

COMPLEXITY, AND RISING ROI EXPECTATIONS ARE MAKING MEASURABLE DELIVERY
HARDER. LEARN WHAT HIGH-PERFORMING TEAMS DO DIFFERENTLY [14]

articles.title: Native all the way, until you need text
articles.description:
Native Apple development frameworks like SwiftUI and AppKit are often
not enough for building complex, text-heavy chat interfaces, leading
devs to favor web-based platforms like Electron for their better rich
text rendering and out-of-the-box performance.

articles.title: Ai is technology, not a product
articles.description:
AI is an essential underlying technology that will eventually pervade
all Apple devices rather than manifest as a standalone "killer
product" that replaces the iPhone ecosystem.

articles.title: Apple silicon costs more than openrouter
articles.description:
Running LLMs locally on Apple Silicon hardware is much more expensive
and slower than using cloud services like OpenRouter due to high
hardware depreciation costs compared to the price per million tokens.

articles.title: Why i don't chain everything in javascript anymore
articles.description:
Transitioning from complex JavaScript method chains to explicit,
step-by-step logic improves code readability, simplifies debugging,
and avoids the performance costs of unnecessary data processing.

articles.description:

articles.title: Bottleneck in clickhouse
articles.description:
Cloudflare's shift to per-tenant retention in a massive ClickHouse
“Ready-Analytics” table exposed an unexpected scaling limit: query
planning, not I/O or scan volume, became the bottleneck as parts per
replica grew. Tracing showed 45% of leaf query CPU time in part
filtering. Switching to a shared lock and then a shared-read cache
removed most of the contention and cut query latency sharply.

articles.title: Viaduct 1.0 and the future of airbnb's data mesh
articles.description:
Viaduct 1.0 is Airbnb's open-source data-oriented service mesh built
on GraphQL. It provides a single unified schema for accessing any data
source across the company while enabling decentralized development
through multi-tenant modules as teams contribute their own schema and
resolvers without operating separate GraphQL services, striking a
balance between a monolithic GraphQL server and full federation.

articles.title: Aws outage may 2026: lessons for database disaster recovery
articles.description:
A major AWS US-EAST-1 outage in May was triggered by a data center
overheating event in a single availability zone, causing multi-hour
disruptions for high-profile services like Coinbase. The incident
highlighted the critical difference between Multi-AZ high availability
(which failed to protect latency-sensitive workloads) and true
cross-region disaster recovery.

articles.title: Exploring schema evolution with ontology-driven propagation
articles.description:
A plain-English ontology can act as a runtime access policy that
survives schema evolution, letting an LLM classify columns
column-by-column using row counts, cardinality ratios, and sampled
values. The approach keeps policy separate from pipeline code, but it
does not cover numeric sensitive inferences or cross-column
re-identification.

articles.title: The modern data stack is overcomplicated: data ingestion
articles.description:
Data ingestion looks simple, but the wrong choice can create hidden
costs through broken connectors, schema drift, over-engineering, and
wasted engineering time. The best approach is usually a hybrid:
managed connectors for standard SaaS, streaming only when low latency
truly matters, and custom pipelines for niche or legacy sources.

articles.title: Welcome to order by jungle
articles.description:
PostgreSQL resolves column names and expressions in ORDER BY clauses
in inconsistent ways. For example, bare identifiers (e.g. ORDER BY a)
first look for aliases in the SELECT list, while any expression (e.g.
ORDER BY -a) resolves against the FROM clause, leading to confusing
behaviors with aliases, quoting, GROUP BY, window functions, and
UNION.

articles.title: A data layer that won't make you wait
articles.description:

you can use a data layer that won't make you wait. That's Lakebase.
Learn how Lakebase's fully-managed Postgres database can help you spin
up ideas fast [14], and run agents and apps on one platform. 

 DUCKLAKE-SDK (GITHUB REPO) [15] 

 ducklake-sdk is an alpha Rust/Python SDK for reading and writing
DuckLake tables without running DuckDB. It implements the DuckLake
spec in a Rust core, with Python integrations for Polars, Arrow, and
DuckDB, targeting SQL-catalog metadata plus Parquet storage. Useful
for embedding DuckLake access into apps, pipelines, or engines
directly.

articles.title: Recompute tax
articles.description:

designed to preserve and share session state across GPU clusters. By
moving context directly from NVMe into the AI data path over 800 GbE
RDMA, it targets the “recompute tax” and claims 95%+ better GPU
utilization and about 50% lower cost per token on benchmark workloads.

articles.title: Apache arrow as data interchange
articles.description:
Apache Arrow is rapidly becoming the universal in-memory columnar
format for data interchange across the modern data stack. Instead of
repeatedly serializing, deserializing, and copying data between tools
(Pandas → Spark → databases, etc.), Arrow enables zero-copy
handoff, where systems share the exact same memory layout,
dramatically reducing CPU overhead.

articles.title: What matters in production rag

(recursive, semantic, and structure-aware), robust indexing pipelines
with document registries, content hashing for efficient updates,
alias-based zero-downtime index switching, careful embedding model
management, and strong observability with detailed tracing, chunk
attribution, and retrieval quality metrics.

articles.title: Your ai agent deletes critical data: who is responsible?

accountability and recovery problem: a Replit agent once deleted a
live database, and the real issue was the absence of clear ownership,
guardrails, and rollback. With 86% of IT/security leaders expecting
agents to outrun current controls, governance is a shared
responsibility across architecture, security, legal, and business.
Practical controls like policy boundaries, observability,
human-in-the-loop triage, and explicit recovery mechanisms are
essential to prevent autonomous tools from becoming enterprise-wide
risk.

articles.title: Context pruning: cut llm tokens without losing quality
articles.description:
Context Pruning is the practice of selectively removing low-value
tokens, sentences, or passages from an LLM's input to reduce cost,
latency, and often improve output quality. It includes techniques such
as token-level, sentence/chunk-level, attention-based, and dynamic
layer-progressive pruning, and works best when paired with semantic
caching.

extra network hop on every operation and more services to deploy, but
there are no secrets to steal, no state to preserve, and agents can be

into the main tab bar—already seen in the App Store and Games

including product design, AI tools, strategy, presentations,
networking, portfolio building, and content creation. Key productivity
hacks include building a personal component library before you need
it, using proper file naming conventions, time-boxing exploration to
90 minutes, making critiques asynchronous by default, and using AI
note-taking apps to handle meeting documentation. These strategies
help designers avoid repetitive work, improve organization, and focus
on actual design decisions rather than administrative tasks.

articles.title: The thinking was never just mine
articles.description:

iteration partners than answer machines, helping people explore and
refine ideas far faster than they could alone. Creativity has likely
always been shaped by outside influences — conversations, books,
criticism, memories, and culture — but AI makes that process
unusually visible through prompts and chat histories. What ultimately
makes an idea feel “yours” may not be pure originality, but the
judgment behind it: the consistent pattern of choices, refinements,
rejections, and instincts that shape the final outcome.

articles.title: Know your craft
articles.description:
AI is lowering the barrier to building products, but also making it
easier for people to create systems they don't fully understand,
leading to polished but fragile apps, workflows, and experiences.
Rather than replacing product and UX design, this shift may make those
disciplines more important, since the real challenge is no longer
shipping quickly but building products that are coherent, trustworthy,
and genuinely useful. AI works best as a tool that amplifies existing
expertise — helping with repetitive tasks, research synthesis,
documentation, and workflows. Speed alone has never guaranteed
success. Blindly using AI without understanding simply allows teams
and individuals to fail faster.

articles.title: Kubernetes v1.36: advancing workload-aware scheduling
articles.description:

workload-aware scheduling by splitting the Workload API into a static
template and a new PodGroup API that handles runtime state, enabling
atomic scheduling of entire pod groups rather than individual pods.
The release also added topology-aware scheduling to reduce network
latency in AI/ML workloads, workload-aware preemption that treats pod
groups as single units, Dynamic Resource Allocation support for shared
devices across massive workloads, and native Job controller
integration that automatically creates gang-scheduled workloads for
indexed parallel jobs.

Face ID in favor of Touch ID to achieve a thinner design. According to
reports, the device could be too slim to fit Apple's current Face ID

consistency, accessibility, visual hierarchy, and contextual
information to help visitors navigate smoothly and complete desired
actions. Quality user experiences make visitors more likely to
remember and return to a brand, and build positive associations with
it, ultimately driving conversions and long-term growth. The article
explores core UX design principles and showcases seven websites that
demonstrate effective user experience design in practice.

articles.title: Agentic design system - from chatbot to orchestration
articles.description:

operational infrastructure that AI agents can read, interpret, and act
upon — with human oversight. This shift requires treating components
as contracts that encode not just structure, but intent, constraints,
accessibility rules, and escalation logic. Teams that add semantic
metadata to tokens and build governance frameworks will be better
positioned than those still optimizing for faster component
generation.

articles.title: How to do ux research in the age of ai

struggles to understand the complexity of real human behavior in
specific environments. Contextual research — observing people in
their homes, noticing physical habits, cultural differences, emotional
reactions, and communication patterns — reveals insights that data
alone often misses. Whether studying accessibility needs, older
adults' sense of familiarity, or how people naturally interact with
devices, the most valuable findings come from human interpretation,
empathy, and observation rather than pattern recognition alone.

using a dedicated operator that recognizes window structures and
organizes data into contiguous memory buffers, the system minimizes
overhead and maximizes CPU efficiency for demanding time-series
workloads.

significant new collaboration with the United Therapeutics Corporation
to explore the use of microgravity to develop improved treatments for
rare lung disease. The companies plan to use microgravity's influence
on the structure and crystallization properties of therapeutic
compounds to improve their stability and delivery. This is the first
time a large, publicly traded company is using capital from its own
balance sheet to build and produce a product in microgravity. Up to
now, NASA has subsidized much of the research into the impact of
microgravity on drug development.
